policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Ye exact usury' renders a participle meaning 'lend on interest' either way: qere נֹשִׁים (from נשה) and ketiv נשאים (from נשא, cf. the noun מַשָּׁא) are orthographic variants of the same sense, and the English cannot tell them apart. The verse's only note (Or, deputies) is alternative_rendering on 'rulers' and touches a different word. Base fallback (qere) retained.
ASV 'Also I said' is first person, matching the qere וָאוֹמַר 'and I said'; the ketiv ויאמר would be third person 'and he said', which the English excludes.
